timecoded_text_to_speech.text: When you say, hey, I have high functioning autism, sometimes they just go into normal.
The autism spectrum may have sort of atypical senses of humour. I think I certainly do.
I haven't met anyone on the spectrum who didn't have a sense of humour.
When I'm probably at my resume or cover letter, I'm finding myself frozen to the point of,
do I mention my high functioning autism or not? I lie about it to get jobs. I don't tell them unless it comes up.
They might instantly disregard me on that point alone because they think I'm
would be some weird antisocial freak who would not be able to get along with the other co-workers.
As you can see from watching my video, I am shaded. This is because I want to be a teacher.
They think, oh, he's going to be aggressive. He won't get the students. He can't teach us not on that level.
Obviously I'm from that generation where unless you were low functioning, you weren't diagnosed,
you were just put in there hard to work out, basket.
I used to get up in the morning and I'd put on the suit and tie and I'd put on a mask.
Over the years, I've just found the masks don't fit quite as well as they used to.
When I get home and take the mask off, it takes me longer to recover.
I feel really offended by the autism equals no empathy.
When I was 42, I thought I was going nuts and I thought I had to go into a mental institution
because I didn't understand anybody and people didn't understand me.
I'm always having to adapt to my environment around me, but I feel like nobody's willing to adapt
to help me progress and grow and understand more.

youtube_description:
This video featuring adults talking about their experiences living with autism spectrum disorder, debunking stereotypes sometimes held. They have been working with Heidi Ham on the development of a sustainable living community for adults on the autism spectrum and Heidi spoke about this project on the TEDxPerth stage in 2014. This video was shown prior to her talk.

Heidi's talk can be viewed at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pb8iHaXag8k
youtube_title: Smashing Stereotypes: Adults with Autism by Heidi Stieglitz Ham
